title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page asks which algebraic numbers λ ∈ Q̄ can occur as eigenvalues of Frobenius on the cohomology of a smooth projective variety over F_q, with q = p^n. Grothendieck lists the necessary conditions that the Weil conjectures (then still conjectural, as was integrality) would impose.

The notation is read as follows: Q' is the field of all totally real algebraic numbers, so Q'(i) is the maximal CM field (the union of all CM fields). The margin note 'N.B. q^{1/2} ∈ Q' !' fits this reading, since √q is totally real.

The kept, boxed conditions are:
(1) λ is an algebraic integer.
(2) λ ∈ Q'(i).
(3) λ^2 (or λ) is q^{i/2}-type times u, where u is a unit outside p and an 'absolute unit' (all conjugates of absolute value 1). Equivalently, there is an integer i with |λ_α| = q^{i/2} for every conjugate λ_α.

Condition (4) is struck out and marked 'conséquence de 2 et 3 !!!'. It says that if 𝔭 and its complex-conjugate prime 𝔭' lie over the same prime of Q', then v_𝔭(u) + v_𝔭'(u) = 0. Equivalently v_𝔭(λ) + v_𝔭'(λ*) equals the p-adic valuation of q^i, with v normalised by v(p) = 1. This is just λ·λ̄ = q^i read p-adically.

The integer i is named the weight of λ relative to q. He notes how the conditions and the weight behave when q is replaced by q' = q^m (λ is replaced by λ^m).

In the margin, the subgroup of Q'(i)^* cut out by (3) and (4) is named M(q^n). This is exactly the group of Weil q-numbers, W(q) in later notation. He also remarks that 1), 3), 4) are 'diophantine' conditions while 2) is of a different nature.

Then comes a 'Conjecture forte', with the margin heading 'Th. d'existence de motifs sur F_q': the necessary conditions are sufficient. That is, every Weil q-integer of any weight occurs as a Frobenius eigenvalue of some smooth projective variety over F_q. He adds that this 'probably determines, at least up to multiplicity one, the motivic Galois group over F_q', which he begins to verify on the next sheet.

In modern terms, this is a general-weight Honda–Tate existence statement. It is coupled with the identification of the motivic Galois group over a finite field with the pro-torus whose character group is the Weil-number group.
errors: The boxed formula v_𝔭(λ)+v_𝔭'(λ*) = in/2 seems off by a factor 2 under the stated normalisation v_𝔭(p)=1. Since λλ̄ = q^i = p^{ni}, the sum should be ni. It is in/2 only under a different convention for the weight or for λ² (the line '3) λ² = ...' is ambiguous). This is possibly a slip, or due to the illegible exponent.

Condition 2) (λ in a CM or totally real field) is not independent. For an algebraic λ ≠ 0, |λ_α| = q^{i/2} at every embedding forces λ̄ = q^i/λ compatibly with all embeddings. So Q(λ) is totally real or CM, and 2) follows from 3). The struck-out 4) is likewise redundant, as Grothendieck himself notes.

In 1965 the conditions are themselves conjectural. Integrality was later shown by Deligne (SGA 7), and the archimedean condition is Deligne's 1974 proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Sufficiency in the naive form 'eigenvalue on H^i of some smooth projective variety over F_q itself' needs care: one may need Tate twists and products, as in Milne's treatment.

ideas.what: Characterisation of Frobenius eigenvalues as Weil q-integers of weight i: algebraic integer, lying in the maximal CM field, all conjugates of absolute value q^{i/2}; weight defined relative to q.
ideas.modern_name: Weil q-numbers / Weil integers of weight i
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Grothendieck–Serre correspondence and the standard-conjectures circle; not stated in this form in EGA/SGA as far as I know

ideas.what: The group M(q^n) ⊂ Q'(i)^* of Weil numbers, with Q' the totally real numbers and q^{1/2} ∈ Q'.
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number group W(q) (character group of the Weil-number protorus)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands–Rapoport (1987), Milne ('Motives over finite fields', 1994); also Saavedra Rivano (1972)

ideas.what: 'Conjecture forte': every Weil q-integer occurs as a Frobenius eigenvalue of a smooth projective variety over F_q (existence theorem for motives over F_q).
ideas.modern_name: Honda–Tate theorem (weight 1, abelian varieties), extended to all weights via abelian-variety motives and Tate twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Honda (1968), Tate (1966/1968 Bourbaki); general weight Milne (1994)

ideas.what: The set of Weil numbers determines the motivic Galois group over F_q, at least for multiplicity one.
ideas.modern_name: Motivic Galois group over F_q (resp. F̄_q) as the Weil-number protorus P (pseudo-motivic groupoid)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly formulates the converse to the Weil conjectures for all weights as an 'existence theorem for motives over F_q'. He packages the Weil numbers into a group M(q^n) inside the maximal CM field and links it to the motivic Galois group over F_q. If the dating to 1965 holds, this predates Honda (1968) and Tate's Bourbaki report. It anticipates the Weil-number torus of Langlands–Rapoport and Milne by over two decades.
missed.quote: Conjecture forte : les conditions nécessaires précédentes sont suffisantes. Cela détermine vraisemblablement, au moins en multiplicité simple, le groupe de Galois motivique sur F_q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority: the Weil-number-protorus description of motives over finite fields is usually attributed to Langlands–Rapoport and Milne, and Honda–Tate to Honda and Tate. The page shows Grothendieck had the full-weight, motivic-Galois-group version in mind. However, the folder's dating spans up to ~1977, which weakens the priority claim.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard (Weil numbers, Honda–Tate, Milne's motives over finite fields). What is notable is an explicit, possibly 1965, formulation of the all-weight existence conjecture and of the Weil-number group as the dual of the motivic Galois group over F_q. This is a documented anticipation not usually credited to Grothendieck, though the uncertain dating tempers it.
transcription_corrections: Q' almost certainly denotes the field of totally real algebraic numbers, so Q'(i) is the maximal CM field. This is why 'N.B. q^{1/2} ∈ Q'' is emphasised.
Line 3) probably reads 'λ² = q^i u' (or 'λ = q^{i/2}u'), not 'λ² = q^{i/2}u', which is inconsistent with the boxed |λ_α| = q^{i/2}.
First line: 'variété projective lisse' is more likely 'variété algébrique [projective et lisse] définie sur le corps F_q'; the handwriting is ambiguous.
The weight sentence probably states that the weight of λ relative to q equals the weight of λ^m relative to q' = q^m (weight invariance), rather than 'égal à mi'.
Margin heading reads 'Th. d'existence de motifs sur F_q' (correctly transcribed); it labels the 'Conjecture forte'.
